name: Øresund Bridge
hint: Keep the shipping lane clear. Tall pylons either side of it can carry most of the deck on straight stays.

history.name: Øresund Bridge
history.engineer: Georg Rotne (architect); Ove Arup & Partners, COWI and others
facts: It is only half the crossing: the link dives into a 4 km tunnel via the artificial island Peberholm, keeping clear of Copenhagen Airport and the shipping channel.
Sixteen unexploded World War II bombs were found on the seabed during construction - yet it opened three months early.
Four motorway lanes run on the upper deck and two railway tracks below.
history.why: The longest cable-stayed main span in the world carrying both road and rail - and the link that joined Denmark and Sweden.
history.note: The rail deck arrives with the Iron Road module; this version carries road traffic only.
